focus: Revisit the built navigator and the rejected first generation candidate through the local learning lab

milestones.name: Public evidence and optional semantic search
Search quality and real browser evaluation
Topic navigator and complete evidence cards

components.name: Public content
components.purpose: One approved source of truth for the public biography, employer work, and independent products.
components.input: Typed Markdown pages and project frontmatter.
components.output: Validated content entries shared by cards, case studies, and search.
components.exercise: Compare a project card and its case study. Find the Markdown fields that feed both.
components.explain: Why should private resume files never be included in a broad indexing glob?
components.pitfall: A number without its measurement scope or attribution can misrepresent an achievement.

components.name: Static delivery
components.purpose: Turn content into ordinary HTML so the portfolio is fast and remains readable without JavaScript.
components.input: Astro routes, layouts, content, and CSS.
components.output: Static HTML and assets under dist, served by GitHub Pages.
components.exercise: Run npm run build and inspect dist/index.html. Find the text without running an app server.
components.explain: What is computed while building, and what must run on a visitor's device?
components.pitfall: A larger optional AI bundle is not the same thing as the initial homepage transfer.

components.name: Public knowledge corpus
components.purpose: Convert the public collections into complete, attributed passages with working source anchors.
components.input: Public pages and project case studies only.
components.output: 38 dated or scoped passages in the current knowledge.json build.
components.exercise: Find the Airflow passage in dist/knowledge.json. Check that nonproduction and the exception remain in its text.
components.explain: Why do we preserve complete sections instead of indexing only impressive numbers?
components.pitfall: A short snippet can drop the qualification that makes a claim accurate.

components.name: Precomputed embeddings
components.purpose: Represent public passages with vectors so visitors only need to embed their question.
components.input: Complete passage text and the pinned MiniLM model configuration.
components.output: 384-dimensional normalized vectors plus a corpus hash and configuration metadata.
components.exercise: Inspect one vector's length, then explain why changing public text requires npm run index:search.
components.explain: How is running an already-trained embedding model different from training an LLM?
components.pitfall: Cosine similarity is a ranking signal, not the probability an answer is true.

components.name: Word matching
components.purpose: Find useful sources quickly without requiring a model download.
components.input: A question and public corpus text.
components.output: Ranked original passages or a no-match reason.
components.exercise: Compare the saved LinkedIn and millions-of-records examples in the learning lab.
components.explain: Why can exact terminology outperform semantic similarity for a named technology?
components.pitfall: A shared employer name alone is weak evidence for an unrelated claim.

components.name: Optional embedding worker
components.purpose: Run meaning-based question encoding off the interface thread after an explicit download choice.
components.input: A question in memory and the pinned public model files.
components.output: A local question vector; no inference API request.
components.exercise: Observe requests before and after AI opt-in. Then cancel and keep using a topic.
components.explain: Why use a worker, and why is the model download still a privacy-relevant network event?
components.pitfall: Cached weights can be evicted, and cached weights do not imply zero runtime transfer.

components.name: Hybrid evidence retrieval
components.purpose: Combine word and meaning rankings while keeping exact matches, source scope, and necessary qualifications.
components.input: Question terms, an optional question vector, and passage vectors.
components.output: At most three complete passages, including paired product hypothesis and outcome when needed.
components.exercise: Switch between word and hybrid traces for the product-assumption example.
components.explain: Why can a small native-versus-WASM numerical difference change eligibility near a cutoff?
components.pitfall: A high score on development questions does not prove performance on unseen wording.

components.name: Guided navigation
components.purpose: Provide fast, predictable routes when the visitor chooses a known topic or follow-up.
components.input: A topic or authored contextual question.
components.output: Explicit validated public passage IDs without invoking a model.
components.exercise: Open Founder, then its evaluation follow-up. Find both source IDs in navigator.mjs.
components.explain: How does an explicit follow-up differ from resolving an open-ended conversation pronoun?
components.pitfall: A topic button is authored navigation, not a generated AI answer.

components.name: Source cards and evidence
components.purpose: Make sources easy to scan while keeping the complete original evidence available.
components.input: Ranked or selected passages and templates built from public content.
components.output: Grouped cards, roles, source links, native evidence disclosures, and contextual actions.
components.exercise: Expand a Nielsen card. Identify the public summary, original quote, and exact source link.
components.explain: Why can we collapse a full passage but should not silently remove its qualification?
components.pitfall: A card summary is authored portfolio copy, not model-written prose.

components.name: Request state and cancellation
components.purpose: Keep the newest visitor action authoritative when data or model work finishes late.
components.input: Typed edits, topic choices, worker messages, timeouts, and cancellation.
components.output: Current results and accessible status; stale responses are ignored.
components.exercise: Read the slow-response browser scenarios and trace which request sequence is allowed to render.
components.explain: What can go wrong if a slow earlier search overwrites a later topic choice?
components.pitfall: A model that loaded successfully can still fail during a later inference.

components.name: Evaluation and release checks
components.purpose: Separate retrieval quality, source completeness, browser behavior, and publication correctness.
components.input: 90 labeled questions, navigator tests, real browser runs, and the production-path build.
components.output: Scoped regression evidence, source integrity checks, and enforced performance budgets.
components.exercise: Explain one answerable, one scope, and one unsupported case without treating them as the same metric.
components.explain: Why is a source appearing in the top three different from every returned sentence being correct?
components.pitfall: Tests used during debugging are regression cases, not independent held-out evidence forever.

components.name: Calendar and deployment automation
components.purpose: Refresh public contribution data and publish a tested exact revision without visitor-time GitHub requests.
components.input: Public calendar data and the source commit.
components.output: A validated snapshot and GitHub Pages artifact, preserving the last valid calendar on failure.
components.exercise: Trace how a bot calendar commit reaches deployment in the same workflow.
components.explain: Why should a visitor request not depend on a live GitHub fetch?
components.pitfall: GitHub Pages ignores public/_headers; document CSP is not a custom worker response policy.

components.name: Grounded answer generation
components.purpose: Test whether a small instruction model can write concise supported answers from retrieved evidence.
components.input: A question, complete public passages, and explicit citation and scope instructions.
components.output: First candidate rejected: 0/8 automated passes in native and browser runs, with manually confirmed source-fidelity failures. No visitor feature is enabled.
components.exercise: Read the reviewed parity, pending-design, and investigation failures in results-summary.json. Explain how each changes the meaning of its source without rerunning the model.
components.explain: What does RAG add after retrieval, and why does a citation alone not prove support?
components.pitfall: Fluent text or valid citation syntax can still misrepresent the source.

components.name: Open-ended follow-up memory
components.purpose: A later experiment could resolve follow-ups using the current conversation while keeping facts grounded.
components.input: A new question and bounded in-memory context.
components.output: Not implemented. Requires a separate scope and evaluation decision.
components.exercise: Compare the explicit question on a current follow-up button with an ambiguous question such as What did he own there?
components.explain: Which information would need to be carried forward, and when should it be cleared?
components.pitfall: Persisting visitor conversations would change the current privacy contract.
